correctness.rationale: For an agent-1 action of type i and each column type j, every element of P_i intersection Q_j must be realized using the e_j actions of type j because column neighborhoods partition U. This forces e_j>=q_ij; symmetrically d_i>=q_ij. Given all inequalities, the outcome h_ij((a+b) mod q_ij) has every cross-cell symbol in each row and column, achieving all bounds. Every realizing table uniquely factors into independent cell rectangles, each with full row/column color coverage, yielding the product of T(q,a,b). Inclusion-exclusion over omission events proves the explicit T formula. The standalone checker reconstructed the constructions over 21297 positive matrices and verified T counts independently on six small samples; finite verification is not used as a universal proof. All quantifiers, q>=1 cases, one-block endpoints, labels, and determinism have been checked.

value.rationale: A resource-minimization problem left open by qualitative and worst-case actual-effectivity representation is solved completely for a natural subclass: all feasible action multiplicity vectors, unique coordinatewise optimum, explicit simultaneous optimizer, and exact labeled outcome-table census. Heterogeneous cross-intersections make the result distinct from homogeneous Latin-square cases. The complete structural classification is suitable as a reference for constrained concurrent-game encoding and resource-aware representation.
